STEP 1 - Scene: A glass of milk on a white surface, photographed from a fairly high oblique angle. It is a drink, not a meal, but the single visible item is milk.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The reference is the printed color checker card, about 8 cm wide (roughly 8 x 8 cm). The glass is a stemless tumbler about 8 cm in diameter at the widest point and about 9 cm tall, with milk filling it to roughly 7-8 cm.

STEP 3 - Items: Whole milk (white, slightly foamy at the rim).

STEP 4 - Area: The milk surface is the glass opening, about 50 cm^2 (diameter ~8 cm). The milk covers the full interior cross-section of the glass, so the milk is the entire visible food.

STEP 5 - Volume: Glass interior ~50 cm^2 x 7.5 cm height ≈ 375 ml. Taper of a stemless tumbler reduces this somewhat; use ~320 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Milk density ~1.03 g/ml. 320 ml x 1.03 ≈ 330 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Whole milk ~61 kcal/100 g. 330 g x 0.61 ≈ 201 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A standard glass of milk (~250 ml) is about 150-160 kcal. A 330 g estimate for a nearly full tumbler is plausible, and 200 kcal sits at the upper end. Estimate: roughly 300 g and about 185 kcal, which is a more reasonable central value for the visible volume.

Final estimate: about 300 g of whole milk, about 185 kcal.
